BatchCreateIngestionBatchItems.name: BatchCreateIngestionBatchItems
BatchCreateIngestionBatchItems.title: Add items to a batch
BatchCreateIngestionBatchItems.documentation:
Adds up to 10,000 more items to a batch that is still `draft`, with a result for each.

A batch takes at most 100,000 items, at most 1,000 of them with `fetchUrl`. The call returns 200
even when every item fails: `results` has one entry per item, in request order, each `created` with
the item, or `failed` with a problem (for example 422 `BATCH_ITEM_CONTENT_AMBIGUOUS`). One bad
item never refuses the rest. A batch that is not `draft` is refused with 409 `CONFLICT`.

input.documentation: The batch to add to.

input.documentation: The items, at most 10,000.

input.name: last
input.documentation:
True when these are the last items: the batch then stops taking items and is planned.
Defaults to false.

The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

BatchDeleteDocuments.name: BatchDeleteDocuments
BatchDeleteDocuments.title: Delete many documents
BatchDeleteDocuments.documentation:
Deletes up to 100 documents in one call, with a result for each.

Each document is deleted as DeleteDocument deletes one. The call returns 200 even when every
item fails: `results` has one entry per identifier, always in request order, each either
`accepted` (the document is now `deleting`, or already was) or `failed` with a code: `NOT_FOUND`
for a document that is gone or that the caller may not see, or `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` when it could
not be marked for deletion; try that one again. A document still being processed is deleted like
any other. One failed item never stops the others. More than 100
identifiers, none, or the same identifier twice is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` for the
whole call. Safe to repeat: a repeat gives the same results, apart from `NOT_FOUND` for documents
that finished deleting in between.

CancelDocumentProcessing.name: CancelDocumentProcessing
CancelDocumentProcessing.title: Stop processing a document
CancelDocumentProcessing.documentation:
Stops the work running on a document: its ingestion, a fill-in or reprocessing.

A stopped first version removes the document; a stopped new version leaves the current one
serving. Until stopping running work is built, every call is refused with 409 `CONFLICT` ("This
document's processing can't be stopped yet"), so callers can build against it now.

Needs the files update permission. Stopping a first version removes the document, so it also
needs the files delete permission, and a caller without it is refused with 403
`PERMISSION_DENIED`. The server checks this, because the permission trait follows input members,
not the document's state.

input.name: knowledgeBaseId
input.documentation: The knowledge base the document is in.

input.name: documentId
input.documentation: The document whose work to stop.

output.documentation:
The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion

The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: etag
output.documentation: The document's ETag.

CancelIngestionBatch.name: CancelIngestionBatch
CancelIngestionBatch.title: Cancel an ingestion batch
CancelIngestionBatch.documentation:
Cancels an ingestion batch.

items already being ingested are stopped too: a stopped new document is removed, and a stopped new
version leaves the current one serving. Otherwise, work already being ingested finishes. Returns
202 with the batch, which becomes `cancelled` once nothing is left running. A final batch is
refused with 409 `CONFLICT`.

input.documentation: The knowledge base the batch belongs to.

input.name: ingestionBatchId
input.documentation: The batch to cancel.

input.name: stopRunning
input.documentation: True stops ingestion already running too; false (the default) lets it finish.

quote it to support.

seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.documentation: The batch's new ETag.

CancelIngestionBatchItem.name: CancelIngestionBatchItem
CancelIngestionBatchItem.title: Cancel a batch item
CancelIngestionBatchItem.documentation:
Cancels one item of a running batch that is still waiting for its upload.

The item becomes `cancelled`, and the document the batch reserved for it is released: a new
document's placeholder is removed, and an existing document is no longer held for a new version.
Bytes already uploaded for it are never ingested. The rest of the batch carries on; if this was the
last item not yet finished, the batch ends. An item that is not `awaiting_upload` (being ingested,
already finished, or in a batch not yet started) is refused with 409 `CONFLICT`. Needs the same
permission as cancelling the batch, and the caller must be able to see the item's folder (404
otherwise).

input.documentation: The batch the item is in.

CancelOperation.name: CancelOperation
CancelOperation.title: Cancel an operation
CancelOperation.documentation:
Cancels an Operation's work.

Work not started yet is dropped; work running is stopped. Only `document_ingestion` can be
cancelled today: a cancelled first version removes the document, and a cancelled new version
leaves the current one serving. Any other kind is refused with 409 `OPERATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE`,
and a final Operation with 409 `CONFLICT`. Returns the Operation, which becomes `cancelled` once
the work has stopped.

Needs the files update permission. For `document_ingestion` the server also checks, on the
document the Operation reads, the permission that started it (`files.create` for a new document,
`files.update` for a new version or a retry) and the document's readers. A caller without it
gets 404, as for an Operation it may not see.

input.name: knowledgeBaseId
input.documentation: The knowledge base the Operation's work is on.

input.name: operationId
input.documentation: The Operation to cancel.

output.documentation:
The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion
output.documentation:
The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: operation
output.documentation: The Operation as it stands after the request. It is the whole response body.

CompareAgentVersions.title: Compare versions
CompareAgentVersions.documentation:
Compares two versions of an agent, member by member.

Returns one change per member that differs, from `version` to `with`, each with its value before
and after; `before` is absent for a member `with` added, and `after` for one it removed. Lists are
compared by their items' keys, so a path reads `workflow.phases[intake].transitions`. Both versions
need the same access as reading them.

input.name: version

input.name: withVersion

CompleteIngestionBatchUploads.name: CompleteIngestionBatchUploads
CompleteIngestionBatchUploads.title: Report finished uploads
CompleteIngestionBatchUploads.documentation:
Reports that items' bytes are in place, so they can be ingested.

Takes 1 to 100 item identifiers, each awaiting upload. For each, the server checks that the
uploaded object's stored SHA-256 and size match the item's, and that the caller may still write to
the item's folder, then starts its ingestion. Returns 200 with a result for each item, in request
order: `accepted`, or `failed` with `CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` (the object is deleted; upload it again),
`NOT_FOUND` (nothing was uploaded to the item's key), `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `UPLOAD_EXPIRED` or
`CONFLICT` (the item is not awaiting upload). One failed item never stops the others. The SDKs
always call this for you. An upload nobody reports is found by the server within about a minute,
while the batch has items awaiting upload, and goes through the same checks; only an item whose
bytes are still missing when its reservation ends fails, with `UPLOAD_EXPIRED`.

input.documentation: The knowledge base the batch belongs to.

input.name: ingestionBatchId
input.documentation: The batch the items are in.

input.name: itemIds
input.documentation: The items whose bytes are in place: 1 to 100, each at most once.

output.documentation:
The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion
output.documentation:
The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: results

CreateDocument.name: CreateDocument
CreateDocument.title: Add a document
CreateDocument.documentation:
Creates a document from an upload; ingestion continues after the response.

Returns 202 with the document in its initial state and the Operation that tracks ingestion, and
`Location` names the document: read it with GetDocument, or wait for it with the SDKs'
`wait()`. Metadata sent here is written with the document before ingestion starts, so
even the first ingestion keeps it. Needs the files permission, read access to the knowledge base
and access to the folder; it does not need update access to the knowledge base, which is for the
knowledge base's own configuration.

input.name: sourceUrl
input.documentation:
The address a citation of this document links to: `https`, at most 2,048 characters. Changing
it needs no processing.

input.name: externalId
input.documentation:
The caller's own key for the document, unique within the knowledge base. A key another document
has is refused with 409 `ALREADY_EXISTS`.

input.name: metadata
input.documentation:
Values for the metadata fields the knowledge base defines. Each value is checked against its
field's definition and the whole request is refused with 422 when any is wrong:
`METADATA_FIELD_UNDEFINED`, `METADATA_VALUE_INVALID` or `METADATA_FIELD_PASSAGE_SCOPED`, each
with a JSON pointer. A value set here is kept as sent: processing never replaces it.

input.name: extraMetadata
input.documentation:
Keys the knowledge base does not define, within the limits on ExtraMetadata; breaking one is
refused with 422 `METADATA_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

input.name: knowledgeBaseId
input.documentation: The knowledge base to add the document to.

input.name: idempotencyKey
input.documentation:
Makes the request safe to retry. The SDKs generate one per call when the caller does not
supply one.

input.name: uploadId
input.documentation:
The upload holding the document's bytes. Each upload can be used once. Refused with 400
`VALIDATION_FAILED` when the bytes are not the file type the document's name says.

input.name: folder
input.documentation: The folder to put the document in.

input.name: name
input.documentation:
What the document is called in the knowledge base and in citations. Absent means the
uploaded file's name. A name without an extension is given the one the upload's content
type maps to, because ingestion reads the file type from it. Refused with 400
`VALIDATION_FAILED` when the type maps to no extension, or when the extension is one a
knowledge base cannot ingest.

output.documentation:
The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion
output.documentation:
The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: location
output.documentation: The document, as `/api/v3/knowledge-bases/{knowledgeBaseId}/documents/{documentId}`.

output.name: etag
output.documentation: The document's ETag; send it as `If-Match` to change it.

output.documentation: The document in its initial state.

CreateDocumentVersion.name: CreateDocumentVersion
CreateDocumentVersion.title: Replace a document's file
CreateDocumentVersion.documentation:
Adds new bytes to a document as a new version; ingestion continues after the response.

The new version becomes the current one once it is indexed; until then the current version keeps
serving search. The bytes must be the same file type as the document's: another type is refused
with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`, because a new type is a new document. While a version is still
processing, another is refused with 409 `DOCUMENT_INGESTION_IN_PROGRESS` and `Retry-After`. Bytes
the same as the current version's make no new version (`result: unchanged`); bytes the same as an
earlier version's bring that version back (`result: restored`).

input.name: documentId

input.documentation:
Makes the request safe to retry. The SDKs generate one per call when the caller does not
supply one.

input.name: ifMatch
input.documentation: The document's ETag. When given, a document that has changed since is refused with 412.

CreateIngestionBatch.name: CreateIngestionBatch
CreateIngestionBatch.title: Create an ingestion batch
CreateIngestionBatch.documentation:
Makes an ingestion batch for one knowledge base, and plans it unless more items will follow.

Takes up to 10,000 items; add more with BatchCreateIngestionBatchItems while `awaitMoreItems` is
true. Returns 202 with the batch, and `Location` names it; wait for the plan with the SDKs'
`batch.planned()`. Needs the ingestion create permission and read access to the knowledge base,
as v2's ingestion route does. A batch that needs bytes uploaded also needs the files create
permission to be started with StartIngestionBatch, which hands out the upload policy; a batch that
needs none runs without that call under `start: when_planned`. A `fetchUrl` item needs the files
create permission when it is added, which the server checks, because the trait cannot follow an
item's member.

Each item that removes a document (`remove`, or an overwrite) is checked by the server for the
files delete permission, and each item that moves one, or adds a new version of one, for the files
update permission, and the token's scope covers it too. An item that fails the check is marked
`failed` with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and the rest carry on. This holds whether the batch starts
through StartIngestionBatch or by itself under `start: when_planned`, so the permission is checked
per item, not once on the call.

input.name: idempotencyKey
input.documentation:
Makes the request safe to retry. The SDKs generate one per call when the caller does not
supply one.

input.name: knowledgeBaseId
input.documentation: The knowledge base to ingest into. It must be `ready`.

input.name: start
input.documentation: When the batch starts once it is planned. Defaults to `when_planned`.

input.name: awaitMoreItems
input.documentation:
When true, the batch stays `draft` and takes more items until it is set false. Defaults to
false.

input.name: policy
input.documentation: The rules that resolve each item's outcome.

input.name: scope
input.documentation: When set, every item must lie inside this folder.

DeleteDocumentVersion.name: DeleteDocumentVersion
DeleteDocumentVersion.title: Delete a document version
DeleteDocumentVersion.documentation:
Deletes one version of a document that is neither current nor processing.

The version, its passages and its renders are removed; its bytes are kept while another version
or document has the same ones. The current version and a version still processing are refused with
409 `CONFLICT`; to remove the current version, delete the document. Like every change, it is
audited.

versions to be numbered already: until they are, a number is refused with 409
`VERSIONS_NOT_NUMBERED`, because deleting would shift every later number; try again later.

`VALIDATION_FAILED`, because the version they name changes after each delete, so a retried
request could delete a second version.

GetAccess.name: GetAccess
GetAccess.title: Get access
GetAccess.documentation:
Gets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

Without `folder` or `document`, the knowledge base's role grants (`roles`). With `folder`, that
folder's `readers`; with `document`, that document's. `inheritedFrom` names the folder whose readers
apply when they are inherited. A folder or document the caller may not see is 404. The root
folder (`folder=/`, `kb.folders('/').access`) holds the readers every folder falls back to; its
readers are never inherited.

PublishAgentVersion.name: PublishAgentVersion
PublishAgentVersion.title: Publish a version
PublishAgentVersion.documentation:
Publishes a version: live then points at it.

Called on `draft`, it first keeps the draft as a new version named `name`, then points live at it,
so live always names a version. The publish permission alone is enough for both: publishing the
draft needs no permission to create versions, which SaveDraftVersion needs to keep a version
without making it live. Called on a named version, it points live at that version, which
rolls back when live pointed at it before: nothing is copied, and the history entry's `kind` is
`rollback`. Versions never change once made, so live answers exactly as the version it names.

Two publishes cannot silently overwrite each other when the caller says what it expects live to
be: `expectedLive` names the version (or `none` before the first publish), or `If-Match` carries
live's ETag. Either, when stale, is refused with 412; with neither, the publish applies to live as
it is. Returns live, the version published, and the history entry the publish wrote.

PutAccess.name: PutAccess
PutAccess.title: Set access
PutAccess.documentation:
Sets who may use a knowledge base, or who may read a folder or a document in it.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it the write is unconditional and the last writer wins, which is
safe because the caller sends the whole list. With it, access that changed since is refused with
412.

Without `folder` or `document`, send `roles`: the roles sent become the whole list. With `folder` or
`document`, send `readers`; `kind: inherit` makes it follow its folder again. The knowledge base's
role grants are set only without a target, under the knowledge base's own permission, as v2's
knowledge base permissions route sets them, so `roles` with `folder` or `document`, `readers`
without one, and both `folder` and `document` are refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. The root folder
(`folder=/`) holds the readers every other folder falls back to, so `inherit` is refused there
with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Applying readers to
the passages a folder or document holds continues after the response; the returned access says
what is set, and the knowledge base's watch shows the work.

Setting `roles` is refused in two cases, as in v2. A caller may give a role only a grant it
could make itself: any other is refused with 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`. And a grant that is not
safe for guests, given to a role that guests or anonymous visitors use, is refused with 422
`RBAC_NOT_GUEST_SAFE`. Only the grants being added are judged, so a grant the role already holds
never blocks an unrelated change. Both checks are made by the server on the roles sent.

ifMatch.reason: The caller sends the whole readers or roles list, so an unconditional write leaves exactly what was sent. Send If-Match to be sure no one changed the access first.

SendMessage.name: SendMessage
SendMessage.title: Send a message
SendMessage.documentation:
Sends a message and streams the answer as server-sent events.

The message is sent when the call is made, whether or not anyone reads the stream. The stream ends
with exactly one `message.completed` or `message.failed`. If the connection drops, the SDK
re-attaches with `WatchConversation` and `Last-Event-ID`, so no event is lost or repeated. Not retried automatically: a send that fails before the stream starts is
reported to the caller.

A message may carry documents in `attachments`, each named by an upload reserved for this
conversation. The SDKs also take files there: each file is uploaded for the conversation first,
and the message is sent once every upload has arrived.

Only a participant may send: whoever started the conversation, or someone it is shared with for
writing (the update grant), who may still see the conversation's agent and holds that agent's
version access grant (the conversation's version may be `live`). A caller without any of
these gets 404, so revoking someone's access to the agent stops them chatting in conversations
they already started.

input.name: context

stored on the conversation.

input.name: attachments
input.documentation:
Documents the message carries. The answering agent version's `attachments.maxFiles`
limits the whole conversation: a message carrying more than `maxFiles` on its own is
refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` at `/attachments`, and an upload that would take the
conversation over its limit with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` at `/attachments/N/uploadId`.
Each upload must be the caller's, reserved for this conversation (CreateUpload with
`purpose.conversationId`), received and not yet used; otherwise the call is refused with
400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` at `/attachments/N/uploadId`. Each upload is used up when the
message is saved.

StartIngestionBatch.name: StartIngestionBatch
StartIngestionBatch.title: Start an ingestion batch
StartIngestionBatch.documentation:
Starts a planned ingestion batch, and returns the upload policy for the items that need bytes.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it, the batch starts as it stands; with it, a batch that changed
since that ETag is refused with 412. A stale plan is planned again first. Each item's write is then checked and
claimed: a new document is reserved at its path, and an existing one is protected by its own
version, so a document that changed since the plan becomes a `changed_since_plan` conflict. An item
the caller may not write is marked `failed` with `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and the rest carry on; the
call still answers 202. Refused with 409
`INGESTION_BATCH_UNRESOLVED` while any item is `unresolved`. Returns 202 with the batch and one
upload policy: list the items to upload with `filter[status][eq]=awaiting_upload`, upload each to
its `objectKey`, then report them with CompleteIngestionBatchUploads.

Each item that removes a document (`remove`, or an overwrite) is checked by the server for the
files delete permission, and each item that moves one, or adds a new version of one, for the files
update permission, and the token's scope covers it too. An item that fails the check is marked
`failed` with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and the rest carry on. This holds whether the batch starts
through StartIngestionBatch or by itself under `start: when_planned`, so the permission is checked
per item, not once on the call.

ifMatch.reason: Starting acts on the batch as it stands, and each item's write is checked against its document when it is claimed, so nothing is overwritten unseen. Send If-Match to start only the plan that was read.

input.documentation: The knowledge base the batch belongs to.

input.name: ingestionBatchId
input.documentation: The batch to start.

input.name: ifMatch
input.documentation:
The batch's ETag, as read after planning. When given, a batch that changed since is
refused with 412; when absent, the batch starts as it stands.

The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.documentation: The batch, now `running`.

output.documentation: The policy every item that needs bytes is uploaded with. Absent when no item needs bytes.

WatchConversation.name: WatchConversation
WatchConversation.title: Watch a conversation
WatchConversation.documentation:
Watches a conversation: the answer being written, if any, then every answer after it, until the
caller closes the stream. An answer whose stream ended moments before the watch opened may still
be delivered, from its `message.started` event; match answers on your own message ID.

Opened without `Last-Event-ID` while an answer is being written, the watch replays that answer
from its start, so it shows the answer so far. An answer too long for the replay buffer cannot be
replayed: the watch sends `stream.reset` instead, then the answers after it. Read the turn with
ListMessages once it ends.

With `Last-Event-ID`, it resumes from the event after that one, so a dropped connection loses
nothing; the SDKs use this to re-attach to `SendMessage`, and to reconnect a dropped watch. When
the answer that event belongs to has ended, or can no longer be replayed, the watch sends
`stream.reset` with a new cursor instead, then carries on. Each answer ends with
`message.completed` or `message.failed`, which end that answer but not the stream, so
helpers watch for the event they need and then close.

input.name: conversationId
input.documentation: The conversation whose answer to re-attach to.

input.name: lastEventId
input.documentation: The `id` of the last event received. Absent means from the start of the answer.

output.name: requestId
output.documentation:
The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion
output.documentation:
The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: events
output.documentation: The rest of the answer, as a stream of `ConversationEvent` events.

WatchKnowledgeBase.name: WatchKnowledgeBase
WatchKnowledgeBase.title: Watch a knowledge base
WatchKnowledgeBase.documentation:
Watches a knowledge base, or one document, folder or batch in it: a snapshot first, then each
change.

Every connection starts with `snapshot`: the thing watched as it stands, its running and recently
finished jobs, and the progress of each document being processed. Then one event per change. A
reconnect needs no cursor, because it starts with a snapshot again; nothing is replayed and
nothing is lost. The SDKs build every scope's `watch()` and `wait()` on this: `wait()` returns once
no job on the thing is running, or raises the error of the job that failed. Events name a document
only to callers who may read it. The server ends the stream after at most an hour, and the SDKs
reconnect.

What the caller needs depends on what it watches. The whole knowledge base needs the knowledge
base read permission and the files list permission, because the snapshot returns the knowledge
base and the documents' progress. One document or folder needs the files list permission. One
batch needs the ingestion list permission, because the snapshot returns the batch.

input.name: knowledgeBaseId
input.documentation: The knowledge base to watch.

input.name: document
input.documentation: Only this document's events.

input.name: folder
input.documentation: Only events about this folder and what is in it, for example `/hr/`.

input.name: batch
input.documentation: Only this ingestion batch's events, and its documents'.

The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion
output.documentation:
The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: events
output.documentation: The events, as a stream of `KnowledgeBaseEvent` events.

WatchOperation.title: Watch an operation

The stream sends `operation.updated` on each change and ends with `operation.finished`. With
`Last-Event-ID`, a dropped connection resumes without losing a change.

WatchWorkspaceEvents.name: WatchWorkspaceEvents
WatchWorkspaceEvents.title: Watch the workspace
WatchWorkspaceEvents.documentation:
Streams the workspace's events the caller asks for, from a cursor or from now.

A stream listens to what it names and nothing else: give `type`, `conversationId`, or both.
Every event is about a subject (a conversation, for now), and the caller receives it only when
it may read that subject, decided per event as a read of the subject would be: the same
permission and, for a token, the same scope. An answer, a tool call or an input request needs
what `WatchConversation` needs; a token whose scopes leave out conversation transcripts receives
none of them.

Each event's `id` is a cursor. Send it back as `after` (or `Last-Event-ID` on a reconnect) to
carry on from it without missing or repeating an event; without either, the stream starts now.
A cursor the stream cannot carry on from is answered with `stream.reset` and a new cursor, not
an error. To wait for something your own call will cause, open the stream first, then make the
call.

Catching up after a cursor covers activity through the v3 API. A conversation event comes
with its content, in the same structures as the conversation's own stream.

input.name: types
input.documentation: The event types to receive.

input.name: conversationIds
input.documentation: The conversations to receive events about.

input.name: after
input.documentation: Carry on after this event. Absent means from now.

input.name: lastEventId
input.documentation: The `id` of the last event received, sent by a reconnecting client in place of `after`.

output.name: requestId
output.documentation:
The identifier support uses to find this request. The same value is in every error body;
quote it to support.

output.name: apiVersion
output.documentation:
The server's model version, for example `5.120.0`. The SDKs keep the latest value they have
seen and refuse to call operations or send members newer than it.

output.name: events
output.documentation: The events, as a stream of `WorkspaceEvent` events.

Agent.documentation: An agent: its name, description, avatar and which version is live.

members.name: id
members.documentation: The identifier every call about this agent takes; it never changes.

members.name: name
members.documentation: What people see the agent called, in the app and in chat. Not versioned.

members.name: description
members.documentation:
What the agent is for. Not versioned. Where a version's handover readers find no description of
their own, they use this one.

members.name: avatar
members.documentation: How the agent looks in lists and in the chat. Not versioned.

members.name: liveVersion
members.documentation: The version live points at. Absent until the agent's first publish.

members.name: createdAt

members.name: updatedAt

AgentAvatarInput.documentation: How an agent should look, as a caller sets it.

members.name: colour
members.documentation: The colour behind the avatar's icon, picture or initials.

members.name: mark
members.documentation: What the avatar shows: a named icon, or a picture.

AgentConfiguration.documentation:
An agent version's configuration: everything about how the agent behaves that a version holds.

The agent's name, description and avatar belong to the agent and are not versioned; who may use
the draft and saved versions belongs to the versions' access grant. A configuration is at most
256 KiB as UTF-8 JSON; anything larger is refused with 400 `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE`.

members.name: guidance
members.documentation:
Who the agent is and how it behaves, and the text it follows at particular points in an
answer. Always present when read.

members.name: models
members.documentation: The model for each job in an answer. A job left unset uses its default.

members.name: knowledgeBases
members.documentation: The knowledge bases the agent searches, and how hard, at most 50, each at most once.

members.name: policies
members.documentation:
The policies the agent's policy reviews and checked phases use, at most 20. Exported as a
template variable.

members.name: connectors
members.documentation: The workspace's connectors the agent may use, at most 20. Exported as a template variable.

members.name: workflow
members.documentation:
The phases a conversation moves through, and how they are grouped. Absent means one
conversational phase, `answer`.

members.name: answers
members.documentation: How answers are shaped: follow-up questions, citations and media embeds.

members.name: conversation
members.documentation: How the chat looks and behaves: the input placeholder and the time zone.

members.name: attachments
members.documentation: Whether people may attach documents in chat, how many and which kinds.

members.name: contentSafety
members.documentation: The guardrail that screens documents attached in chat. Exported as a template variable.

members.name: deniedDocuments
members.documentation:
When true, the answer stream tells the caller which documents were withheld from them.
Defaults to false.

members.name: memory
members.documentation: Whether the agent remembers people between conversations. Absent means it does not.

members.name: voice
members.documentation:
Whether the agent speaks its answers, and in which voice. Absent means the browser's own
voice.

members.name: liveAvatar
members.documentation: A live video avatar that speaks for the agent. Absent means none.

members.name: journey
members.documentation:
The page people see before and while they work through a stepped workflow, such as
onboarding. Absent means the agent has no such page.

members.name: runAs
members.documentation:
Whose permissions the agent's unattended runs use. Exported as a template variable. Absent
means the agent cannot run unattended.

AgentGuidance.documentation: Who the agent is and how it behaves, and the text it follows at particular points in an answer.

members.name: identity
members.documentation:
Who the agent is and whom it serves, at the top of every prompt, at most 4,000 characters.
Absent uses the platform's.

members.name: instructions
members.documentation:
How the agent behaves, at most 100,000 characters. Always present when read; an empty string
means none.

members.name: relevance
members.documentation: What makes an answer relevant to the people this agent serves, and what it should decline.

members.name: definitions
members.documentation: A glossary of terms the agent reads the same way every time.

members.name: searchTopics
members.documentation: How to turn a question into the topics it searches for.

members.name: resultEvaluation
members.documentation:
How to judge the passages a search finds, for example "prefer the most recent". Not used with
the `reranker` evaluation method.

members.name: limitedEvidence
members.documentation:
What to say when the knowledge bases hold too little to answer. When set, it replaces
`instructions` in the reply to a question with no evidence.

AgentMark.documentation: What an agent's avatar shows. Exactly one member is present.

members.name: icon
members.documentation: A named icon from the platform's set.

members.name: pictureUrl
members.documentation:
The uploaded picture's address, to show as an image. It may stop working after a time; read the
agent again for a fresh one.

AgentMarkInput.documentation:
What an agent's avatar should show. Exactly one of `icon` and `pictureUploadId`; both or neither
is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

members.name: icon
members.documentation: A named icon from the platform's set.

members.name: pictureUploadId
members.documentation:
An upload holding the picture, reserved with CreateUpload and `purpose: {agentAvatar: true}`.
Each upload can be used once.

AgentModels.documentation: The model for each job in an answer. A job left unset uses its default.

members.name: answer
members.documentation: Writes the answer. The other jobs fall back to this one's model when their own is unset.

members.name: planning
members.documentation: Plans the answer: reads the question, plans the searches and reads attached documents.

members.name: summary
members.documentation: Summarises a long conversation so the answer stays within the model's limits.

members.name: classification
members.documentation: Decides what kind of message arrived, and whether the question is in scope.

members.name: searchTopics
members.documentation: Writes the search topics for a question. Falls back to `planning`, then `answer`.

members.name: title
members.documentation: Names a conversation, once. Defaults to a small, fast model, not the answer model.

AgentVersion.documentation:
A named version of an agent: `draft`, `live` or a saved version. A list leaves `configuration`
out; read one version to get it.

members.name: agentId
members.documentation: The agent the version belongs to.

members.name: name
members.documentation: `draft`, `live` or the version's name.

members.name: liveVersion
members.documentation: On `live`: the name of the version live points at.

members.name: source
members.documentation: How a named version was made. Absent on the draft.

members.name: basedOn
members.documentation: The version this one was made from, where there is one.

members.name: matchesLive
members.documentation: True on the version live points at, and on `live` itself. Defaults to false.

members.name: createdAt
members.documentation: When the version was made; for the draft, when it was first created.

members.name: createdBy
members.documentation: Who made the version. Absent on the draft and on versions carried over from before v3.

members.name: publishedAt
members.documentation: On `live`: when live was pointed at this version.

members.name: publishedBy
members.documentation: On `live`: who pointed live at this version.

members.name: note
members.documentation: The note written when the version was saved or published.

members.name: changedMembers
members.documentation:
The members that differ from the version this one was made from (`basedOn`); for the draft,
from live. Lists are compared by their items' keys.

members.name: configuration
members.documentation:
The version's configuration. Present on a single read and on the draft operations; absent in
ListAgentVersions rows and in PublishAgentVersion's `version`.

members.name: etag
members.documentation:
The version's current ETag; send it as `If-Match` to change it. On `live`, it changes whenever
live moves to another version.

AgentVersionChange.documentation: One member that differs between two versions.

members.name: path

members.name: before

members.name: after

AgentWorkflow.documentation: The agent's workflow: the phases a conversation moves through.

members.name: entryPhase
members.documentation: The phase a new conversation starts in. Defaults to `answer`, the phase every agent has.

members.name: phases
members.documentation:
The phases, in the order their journey steps are numbered. Always present when read. Lists
are replaced whole: to change one phase, send them all back.

members.name: capabilities
members.documentation:
Groups of phases that each run with their own instructions and only their own tools. Absent:
every phase shares one set of instructions and one set of tools.

members.name: model

model that does not accept it (see `acceptsTemperature` in `GET /v3/models`).

members.name: topK

members.name: maxOutputTokens
members.documentation: The most tokens the job may write, from 1 to 16,384. Defaults to 2,048.

members.name: maxAttempts

members.name: reasoning

members.name: maxContinuations
members.documentation:

members.name: followUpQuestions

members.name: citations

members.name: mediaEmbeds
members.documentation: Whether the agent shows images and media from the passages it cites.

members.name: uploadId

members.name: enabled
members.documentation: Whether people may attach documents in chat. Defaults to false.

members.name: style
members.documentation: How much the voice exaggerates its style, from 0 to 1. Absent uses the provider's default.

Capability.documentation:
A group of phases the agent handles as one area of work. While a conversation is in one of its
phases, the model sees only the capability's instructions and its phases' tools. Moving into a
phase of another capability hands the conversation over, with a summary for the next one.

members.name: id
members.documentation: The capability's identifier, unique within the workflow.

members.name: description
members.documentation: What this capability does, in one sentence. The capability that receives a handover reads it.

members.name: instructions
members.documentation: Added after the agent's instructions while the capability is active.

members.name: phases
members.documentation:
The phases it owns, at least one. When capabilities are declared, every phase belongs to
exactly one.

members.name: conversationScope
members.documentation:
Who a conversation in this capability is shared with. Absent decides nothing: the
conversation keeps its sharing until it enters a capability that sets one.

members.name: documentId

members.name: documentName

members.name: citation

members.name: version

members.documentation: The version of the agent that answers.

members.documentation: The answer has started.

members.name: phaseChanged
members.documentation: The agent moved to another phase of its workflow.

stream ends with it, and a conversation's watch carries on to the next answer.

members.documentation:

ended, or can no longer be replayed. The events after it are never sent; read the
conversation's messages for what was missed, then carry on from the new cursor.

theme's.

members.name: high

members.name: knowledgeBaseId

members.name: name

members.name: folder
